newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension reform bill reading delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension reform bill reading delayed again.

text.p: Brazil's pension reform bill will not be presented to a Senate committee this week as had been expected, a congressional official said.

The latest version of the bill, which has been substantially rewritten to include points lost during lower house voting last year, might now be unveiled in the Constitution and Justice Committee next week, the official said.
"It was decided to wait a bit longer because of the re-election bill," she said.
A bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year was due to be put to a second and final vote in the Senate later Wednesday.
The pension reform bill, along with a civil service reform bill currently stuck in the Chamber of Deputies, is considered crucial to the government's attempts to improve Brazil's fiscal performance.

Among other points, it would set a minimum retirement age for civil servants of 60 for men and 55 for women, scrap some public sector pension perks and tie pensions for all workers to contributions they have made rather than time they have worked.
